executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 reveal multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to pose a significant zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas, with repeated alerts from PAHO indicating ongoing circulation in animal populations. Mpox transmission persists in the Americas region alongside resurgent measles activity, while dengue and chikungunya maintain elevated transmission pressure across the Western Hemisphere. The Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset in April 2026 adds additional respiratory disease burden coinciding with RSV co-circulation.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent epidemic threats including H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk, mpox, dengue surge, and measles resurgence demand coordinated surveillance and response across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Repeated alerts suggest ongoing zoonotic spillover risk to humans from infected animal populations
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential flagged across two separate reporting periods
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; ensure PPE protocols at farms and live bird markets; expedite antiviral stockpiling and pandemic preparedness planning

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating continued transmission in the Americas
Sustained circulation warrants ongoing vigilance following global clade designations
BSL-3 select agent with documented human-to-human transmission chains
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs; ensure laboratory diagnostic capacity; monitor for clade Ib introduction into the Americas

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicates high transmission activity
Historical pattern of record-breaking dengue seasons in the Americas continuing into 2026
Multi-serotype co-circulation increases severe dengue risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; expand surveillance for severe dengue; alert clinicians to increased case burden and potential hemorrhagic presentations

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
threats.location: Americas Region (Southern Hemisphere onset); Northern Hemisphere
signals: PAHO alert April 2026 marks start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
January 2026 alert flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation
December 2025 alert covered Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season start indicating bimodal seasonal pressure
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination campaigns in Southern Hemisphere countries; enhance hospital surge capacity monitoring; strengthen sentinel surveillance for novel influenza variants

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission risk
Declining vaccination coverage in post-pandemic period creates susceptible populations
Risk of imported cases reestablishing endemic transmission in elimination-status countries
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates by district; conduct supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Dual PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicate sustained resurgence
Rising case counts suggest waning immunity from acellular pertussis vaccines
Infants under 6 months remain at highest risk for severe disease and mortality
threats.action: Expand Tdap booster coverage especially for pregnant women and healthcare workers; enhance laboratory confirmation capacity; investigate potential vaccine-escape strain circulation

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Aedes vector co-distribution with dengue increases dual infection risk
Potential for geographic expansion into new areas with competent vector populations
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya surveillance with dengue vector control programs; educate clinicians on differential diagnosis; monitor for potential neurological complications

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert December 2025 indicating HPS cases in the Americas
Case fatality rates for HPS exceed 30-40% with no specific antiviral treatment approved
Rodent reservoir activity and human exposure risk may be modulated by climate and land use changes
threats.action: Issue public health advisories on rodent exposure prevention; ensure healthcare providers can recognize early HPS presentations; maintain ICU capacity for cardiopulmonary support in affected areas

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents were identified in this surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a Tier 1 select agent with pandemic potential — generated two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas and representing the highest-priority biosecurity concern. Monkeypox virus (MPXV), also classified as a BSL-3 select agent, was the subject of a PAHO epidemiological update in April 2026, confirming continued transmission in the Americas region. Both pathogens require enhanced laboratory biosafety protocols, specialized containment measures, and coordinated public health response frameworks.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in this surveillance set; however, pertussis resurgence may warrant macrolide resistance surveillance given Bordetella pertussis treatment protocols
Dengue and chikungunya co-epidemics create conditions for increased antibiotic misuse leading to secondary AMR pressure
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) may indicate broader pharmaceutical supply chain vulnerabilities relevant to antimicrobial access and stewardship
emergingPatterns: Temporal clustering of multiple PAHO alerts between December 2025 and April 2026 suggests a broad-based resurgence of vaccine-preventable and vector-borne diseases in the Americas
Simultaneous H5N1 activity in animals and mpox in humans represents a dual select-agent detection window requiring heightened biosurveillance

Southern Hemisphere influenza season beginning April 2026 overlapping with ongoing dengue and chikungunya transmission creates multi-pathogen respiratory and febrile illness differential diagnosis challenge

Recurring pertussis alerts across consecutive reporting periods (December 2025, March 2026) suggest a sustained resurgence rather than isolated outbreak, possibly reflecting waning vaccine immunity at population level

Non-infectious hazard signals (methanol poisoning, GLP-1 misuse) appearing in epidemiological alert systems indicate expanding scope of public health surveillance beyond communicable disease boundaries
